title: sys_scim_connection_credential: two credentials of one connection cannot be told apart (no token hint, no last use)
body:
repo:cloud#3 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbZqfEd7pcckjz3pGqn

Blocks cloud#4278 (p2, SCIM provisioning console); drafted by the cloud#4278 card thread (session_01JQwxbY3zqaaaSj7tJsov3a) and filed by the seat.

Edition / version: framework pin 99992ddf. Consumer: cloud SCIM provisioning console "Connections" grid and the open Setup → SCIM Credentials list; cloud#4278 item 3.

Measured on cloud#4278 (local SCIM run, two mints for `okta-test`): the two rows show the same connection id, label and created minute, both Active. The documented rotation ("mint a second credential, move the IdP to it, then revoke the old one", the mint action's own `helpText`) cannot be followed safely, because nothing says which row the IdP is using.

Why (code): the object's fields are `connection_id`, `provisioning_domain_id`, `organization_id`, `label`, `token_digest` (internal), `active`, `expires_at`, `user_id`, timestamps. Every bearer starts with the constant `oss_scim_`, so a prefix tells nothing apart; there is no suffix hint. `verifyScimBearerToken` in `plugin-auth/src/scim-connection-service.ts` reads the row by digest and writes nothing back, so there is no last-use time.

Seam: `runtime: scim-connection-service verifyScimBearerToken` → `object: sys_scim_connection_credential` (no consumer field yet).

Expected: (a) a non-secret `token_hint` (e.g. the last 4 characters of the bearer, stored at mint, shown in the mint result dialog too so the admin can match it to what they pasted into the IdP); (b) `last_used_at`, written by the verifier on a successful verify, throttled (e.g. at most once a minute per credential) so a busy IdP does not write on every request. Both readable through the list door, both in the `all` list view. Never the bearer, never the digest.

Dedupe words: "scim credential last_used_at", "scim token hint", "scim rotation which credential", "sys_scim_connection_credential last used".
